### Source and Sustainer of Life
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/source-and-sustainer-life
Passage: John 11:17-27
Points:
- Lazarus had been dead for four days, eliminating natural explanations and setting the stage to display Christ's supernatural power.
- Martha lamented that Jesus was not present earlier, yet she still trusted His unique relationship with the Father.
- Jesus redirected Martha's attention from an abstract, future resurrection to Himself as the living source of life.
- Believers united to Jesus still face bodily death, but death does not possess the final word over their eternal destiny.

### When God Cried
Author: Liz Curtis Higgs
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement/encouragement-for-today-january-18-2019.html
Passage: John 11:35
Points:
- Deep loss often tempts grieving believers to dwell on agonizing "if-only" regrets.
- Jesus did not scold Mary for her tears, but felt genuine anguish and anger toward death's destructive power.
- By openly weeping at the tomb, the Son of God shared intimately in the sorrow of His friends.
- Hurting believers can find comfort knowing Christ meets them in their pain and grieves alongside them.

### It’s Never Too Late for Jesus
Author: Constantine Campbell
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/its-never-too-late-for-jesus
Passage: John 11:20-37
Points:
- Although Martha and Mary greeted Jesus with identical initial words, their postures toward hope differed significantly.
- Martha anchored her sorrow in biblical theology, believing Jesus could still do something even after death.
- Jesus revealed that resurrection is not merely an abstract end-times event, but a living reality embodied in Himself.
- While grief can tempt people to surrender to despair, trusting Jesus reminds us that death never has the ultimate word.

### Jesus Speaks When We Stop to Listen
Author: Beloved Women
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/beloved-women/beloved-women-october-7-2019.html
Passage: John 11:25
Points:
- Martha stepped away from her typical busyness to run out and meet Jesus in her grief.
- By pausing to listen rather than just act, Martha opened her heart to hear divine truth.
- Jesus met her sorrow with the profound revelation that He is the resurrection and the life.
- Making intentional daily space to listen to the Lord provides comfort and enduring hope in painful moments.
